capture_machine: Linux x86_64, Python 3.14.3, sase_core_rs default install
comment: Phase 7E (sase-1e.5) regression-floor baseline. Anchors are the stable subset Phase 7B recommended: parse_project_bytes (golden + synthetic_200), parse_query parse-only direct, scan_agent_artifacts synthetic 6p/200pp scan_facade, and apply_status_update golden_myproj_pure (must-not-regress-further guard, not must-beat-python). The Phase 7B handoff explicitly excluded all Git normalizer surfaces and parse_git_name_status_z because their absolute medians are below 50us and noise alone moves them by more than 25%.

tolerance.comment: Rust median may be up to 40% slower than the Phase 7B captured Rust median before failing. The 40% headroom (above the plan's 25-35% recommendation) covers GitHub-hosted runner variance vs the Phase 7B capture machine; tighten in Phase 7F or later once we have CI history showing the data is stable. The relative 'must_beat_python' check is hardware-independent and runs on the same machine in the same process, so it stays at parity (no slack).

anchors.rationale: Clean ~2.4x Rust win at the smallest realistic input. Both direct and facade tiers beat Python every time Phase 7B was rerun.
~1.4x win on a 200-spec synthetic file. Mirrors what users actually parse and is the largest deterministic parser workload Phase 7B captured.

~2.1x Rust win on direct query parsing (no facade/wire overhead). Phase 7B's evaluate_query_many path is intentionally NOT an anchor because it currently regresses (per-call wire conversion dominates).
~1.21x win on the synthetic 6-project x 200-per-project tree, the closest hermetic ~/.sase/projects approximation Phase 7B captured.

Must-not-regress-further guard, not a must-beat-python anchor. Phase 7B showed Rust at parity with Python on this golden workload (~5.8 vs ~5.6 us); the synthetic_200_specs version regresses by ~30% but is too noisy to anchor on. This anchor catches the case where Rust suddenly drops below the recorded floor on an absolute-time basis.
